answer: Picture the agent economy as an ocean: when one controller floods it with clones, their outputs bleed together like the same pigment in water. Each epoch the network publishes open-ended work items and clusters all solutions by semantic similarity; each cluster's reward is paid once and split among its members. A submission is a cipher only its own private history can cheaply produce, so honest agents rarely cluster, while a hundred clones divide one reward a hundred ways. The attack becomes self-defeating: every extra clone dilutes the others.
